_warning: SYNTHETIC QA FIXTURE. NOT CURATED RESEARCH DATA. DO NOT SHIP.
Every citation here is invented and every region mapping is chosen to
exercise a requirement, not because it is true. The authors are named
'Fixture', the venues are fictional and every source URL is on
example.invalid, so that this file cannot be mistaken for the real seed
dataset even at a glance.
The real ~30-paper seed set is DOG-37's deliverable and will land at
packages/atlas-research/fixtures/. This file exists so the §7 journey is
executable BEFORE that, and the harness prefers the real fixture the
moment one appears — see src/fixture.ts. It is retained after that as the
harness's own self-test input, because a suite whose only input is another
team's deliverable cannot be run when that deliverable is broken.
The five papers are shaped by what the journey has to be able to do:
P-02 is found via BA44 and ALSO maps BA10 and BA13, which is the
DOG-1 §3 filter-leak case and the reason the fixture needs a paper
whose mappings reach outside any plausible filter.
P-01, P-02 and P-04 all map BA44, so two-paper comparison has a real
overlap to hatch and a third selection to distinguish it from.
P-04's F-08 has no spatial detail at all, which must render as an
explicit 'region-level only' marker rather than being interpolated.
P-05 maps a body region as well as a brain one, so a paper's mappings
can span both atlases.
P-03 maps exactly one region, so 'reveals all its regions' is not
accidentally satisfied by a fixture where every paper is multi-region.
_structureNote: The body atlas's brain structure is addressed at BD-C01, the topmost
level the BD frame has. The frame is anchored to the vertebral column and
cannot address above C01 at all, so 'the brain, seen from the body atlas'
is represented by the top cervical cells. That is a real limitation of the
frame rather than of this fixture, and it is the cross-atlas link's job to
carry the user from there into BV. Raised with the CTO on DOG-38.
